s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging, firm, painless mass in the left labia majora with a history of recurrences
salient_findings: Slowly enlarging mass in the left labia majora over 10 years
Firm, painless, immobile mass measuring approximately 7 × 4 cm
History of recurrences after previous excisions
key_facts: 64-year-old woman
Mass in the left labia majora
Mass is firm, painless, and immobile
Mass measures approximately 7 × 4 cm
Normal vital signs
Normal routine laboratory tests
History of excision of a mass in the Bartholin’s gland in 2000
Histopathology in 2007 showed chondroid syringoma
Recurrence in the labia majora was resected with histology showing clear cell hidradenoma
Ultrasound revealed a heterogeneous, hypervascular subcutaneous mass
CT scan demonstrated a heterogeneous, contrast-enhancing lesion in the left labia majora
Low-density focus in the liver suggestive of a simple cyst
Vulvar mass was excised and reported as chondroid syringoma
Recurrence near the fourchette three months after excision

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of multiple recurrences with histopathology consistently showing chondroid syringoma, including the most recent excision of the vulvar mass.

rejected.label: Clear cell hidradenoma
rejected.why: Although one of the recurrences showed clear cell hidradenoma, the majority of the histopathology reports, including the most recent, indicate chondroid syringoma.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no indication of malignancy in the provided histopathology reports, and the patient's masses have been described as benign entities like chondroid syringoma.

rejected.label: Vulvar adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The histopathology reports do not support a diagnosis of adenocarcinoma; instead, they consistently point towards benign tumors like chondroid syringoma.

rejected.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no evidence in the provided case facts to suggest apocrine gland carcinoma, and the described histopathology is not consistent with this diagnosis.
